mainTopic: חנניה מישאל ועזריה and the furnace: the vision of זכריה, the fate of the three and דניאל, and the false prophets burned alongside יהושע כהן גדול
overview: This amud tells more of the story of חנניה מישאל ועזריה, who came out of נבוכדנצר's furnace unharmed. It opens by learning that צדיקים are greater than מלאכי השרת. It then says the miracle shamed the rest of ישראל, who had bowed to the idol. רבי יוחנן explains a vision of זכריה: ה׳ was ready to destroy the world, but He calmed down when He looked at these three צדיקים in בבל. The גמרא then asks what became of the three afterward, and where דניאל was during the furnace story. A ברייתא explains why ה׳, דניאל and נבוכדנצר all wanted דניאל away. Next comes the story of the false prophets אחאב and צדקיה, who were burned in a furnace, while יהושע the כהן גדול, thrown in with them, came out with only singed clothes. The גמרא explains why the fire touched him at all, and what sin he was punished for. The amud ends as בר קפרא begins explaining the 'six barley grains' that בועז gave רות, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The righteous are greater than the ministering angels
steps.stepSummary: צדיקים are greater than מלאכי השרת. The proof is that נבוכדנצר mentions the three people in the furnace before the angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The righteous are greater than the ministering angels. We see this from the פסוק: 'He answered and said: Behold, I see four men unbound, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are not hurt. The fourth one looks like a son of the gods.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that צדיקים rank higher than מלאכי השרת. It brings a פסוק from the furnace story as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the furnace were three צדיקים (חנניה מישאל ועזריה) and one angel. נבוכדנצר first notices the 'men' and only then mentions 'the fourth' who looks divine. The order of the פסוק shows that the צדיקים come first in importance.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
A son of the gods, meaning a divine being or angel

phrases.english: The righteous are greater than the ministering angels,
as it is stated: "He answered and said:
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:25. The one speaking is נבוכדנצר, looking into the furnace.

phrases.english: Behold, I see four men
unbound, walking in the midst of the fire,
and there is no hurt in them;

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵוֵהּ דִּי רְבִיעָאָה דָּמֵה לְבַר אֱלָהִין״.
phrases.english: and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods."
phrases.notes: The 'fourth' is the angel. The three צדיקים are mentioned before him, and that order is the proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדוֹלִים צַדִּיקִים יוֹתֵר מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about חנניה מישאל ועזריה in the furnace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are greater than מלאכי השרת, as shown by the order of the פסוק in דניאל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how highly the גמרא values human צדיקים who stay loyal to the הקדוש ברוך הוא, even above angels.

steps.title: The nations mock Israel after the furnace miracle
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says that after the miracle, the nations shamed ישראל for bowing to the idol. The answer was a פסוק admitting shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says: When חנניה מישאל ועזריה came out of the fiery furnace, all the nations came and slapped ישראל in the face. They said: 'You have a God like this, and you bow down to an idol?!' Right away they answered with the פסוק: 'To You, ה׳, is righteousness, and to us is shame, as on this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement says the miracle also brought shame on ישראל. Most of them had bowed to נבוכדנצר's idol, while only three refused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle proved how powerful the God of ישראל is. That made the sin of the many Jews who bowed to the צלם look even worse. The response does not make excuses. It admits that ה׳ is right and the people are to blame.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The enemies of Israel', a polite way of saying Israel itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of Israel' here does NOT mean real enemies. It is a polite way to avoid saying something bad directly about ישראל. The ones being slapped are ישראל themselves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai says:
At the moment that Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya came out
from the fiery furnace,
all the nations of the world came

phrases.aramaic: וְטָפְחוּ לְשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל פְּנֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: and slapped "the enemies of Israel" on their faces.
phrases.notes: This is a polite way of saying they slapped ישראל themselves.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: יֵשׁ לָכֶם אֱלוֹהַּ כָּזֶה,
phrases.english: They said to them: You have a God like this,
and you bow down to the idol?!
Immediately they began and said:
"To You, ה׳, is righteousness,
phrases.notes: דניאל 9:7

phrases.english: and to us is shame of face, as on this day."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיָּצְאוּ חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה מִכִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the furnace story but turns from praise of the three צדיקים to the shame of the rest of ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The furnace miracle exposed the sin of those who bowed to the צלם. The proper response was to admit guilt.

steps.title: Only one branch of the palm tree was grasped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains a פסוק in שיר השירים‎. ה׳ hoped all of ישראל would pass the test, but only חנניה מישאל ועזריה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the פסוק mean, 'I said, I will climb the palm tree, I will grab its branches'? 'I said, I will climb the palm tree' refers to ישראל. 'But now, all that came up in My hand was one branch: חנניה מישאל ועזריה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא explains a פסוק along the same lines. Out of all of ישראל, only these three stood strong in נבוכדנצר's test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The palm tree stands for the whole Jewish people. ה׳ 'climbed' it to test it, hoping to gather much. In the end He held only one small branch, the three who refused to bow. This adds to step 2: the miracle shows both the greatness of the few and the failure of the many.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (introduces an explanation of a פסוק)
A branch or bough of a palm tree
Nothing came up in my hand, meaning I did not succeed in getting

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says that Rabbi Yonatan says:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"I said: I will climb into the palm tree; I will grasp its branches"?
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:9

phrases.english: "I said: I will climb into the palm tree": this is Israel,
and now nothing came up in My hand
phrases.notes: ה׳ is the one speaking here.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סַנְסַן אֶחָד שֶׁל חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: except one branch: that of Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea of step 2: only these three passed the test, while most of ישראל failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In נבוכדנצר's test, only חנניה מישאל ועזריה stayed loyal. They were the 'one branch' ה׳ held.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks about Zechariah's vision
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a vision from זכריה and asks what it means. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: What does the פסוק mean, 'I saw the night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse, and he was standing among the myrtles that were in the depths'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes a mysterious פסוק from זכריה and asks what it means. This is a setup line: the next steps explain the פסוק piece by piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole פסוק is quoted first so that each phrase can be explained one at a time. The next steps explain 'night', 'a man riding', 'a red horse', and then 'standing among the myrtles in the depths' (steps 8–10).

keyTerms.meaning: The depths, a deep or shadowy place

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"I saw the night, and behold, a man
phrases.notes: זכריה 1:8

phrases.english: riding upon a red horse,
and he stood among the myrtles
that were in the depths, etc."?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new explanation of a פסוק by a different אמורא. It is still part of the same theme of how few צדיקים there were.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the images in זכריה's vision mean?

steps.title: 'I saw the night': ה׳ wanted to turn the world to darkness
steps.stepSummary: The word 'night' shows that the הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to turn the whole world into night.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'I saw the night' mean? The הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to turn the whole world into night.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the first phrase of the פסוק. 'Night' hints that ה׳ wanted to make the whole world dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Night' is read as a sign of darkness and destruction, not just the time of day. ה׳ was ready to bring darkness on the whole world, because there were so few צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: What is meant by "I saw the night"?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted

phrases.aramaic: לַהֲפוֹךְ אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לְלַיְלָה.
phrases.english: to turn the entire world into night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 for the first phrase of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Night' means ה׳ wanted to turn the whole world into darkness.

steps.title: 'A man riding' refers to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The 'man' in the vision is the הקדוש ברוך הוא. The proof is a פסוק that calls ה׳ 'a man of war'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And behold, a man riding': 'man' here means only the הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says, 'ה׳ is a man of war, ה׳ is His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains who the 'man' in the vision is. He proves from a פסוק in שמות that 'man' can mean ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses a matching word. In the song at the sea, ה׳ is called 'a man of war'. So the 'man' riding in זכריה's vision is understood the same way. This tells us that the rider in the vision is ה׳ Himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is nothing other than, meaning 'this word refers only to'

phrases.english: "And behold, a man riding":
"man" means none other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it is stated: "ה׳ is a man of war, ה׳ is His name."
phrases.notes: שמות 15:3

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ רֹכֵב״ – אֵין ״אִישׁ״ אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the next phrase of the פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'man' riding is the הקדוש ברוך הוא, proven from 'ה׳ is a man of war'.

steps.title: 'A red horse': ה׳ wanted to turn the world to blood
steps.stepSummary: The red color of the horse shows that the הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to turn the whole world into blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On a red horse': the הקדוש ברוך הוא wanted to turn the whole world into blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the horse is red. Red stands for blood, meaning ה׳ wanted to bring destruction on the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the idea of 'night' in step 5 with a stronger image, blood instead of darkness. Together, 'night' and 'red' show that ה׳ was ready to destroy the world, because so few people stood up for Him.

phrases.english: "Upon a red horse":
The Holy One, Blessed be He, wanted
to turn the whole world into blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל סוּס אָדֹם״ – בִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַהֲפוֹךְ אֶת הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק from step 4 and matches the 'night' idea of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The red horse means ה׳ wanted to turn the whole world into blood.
steps.whatToRemember: So far in רבי יוחנן's explanation, 'night' and 'red horse' both show that ה׳ was ready to destroy the world, and the 'man' riding is ה׳ Himself. The next step explains what calmed Him.

steps.title: ה׳ calms down when He sees חנניה מישאל ועזריה
steps.stepSummary: Once ה׳ looked at חנניה מישאל ועזריה, His anger cooled. The words 'standing among the myrtles in the depths' show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once ה׳ looked at חנניה, מישאל and עזריה, He calmed down. That is why the פסוק says: 'And he stood among the myrtles that were in the depths.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps explaining זכריה's vision, piece by piece. Now it explains the next words: the 'man' (ה׳) was standing among the myrtles in the depths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 and 7 showed that ה׳ wanted to turn the world into night and blood. This step shows what stopped Him: He looked at the צדיקים. Standing 'among the myrtles' means focusing on those three righteous men.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind cooled down; He was calmed

phrases.english: Once He looked at Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
His mind cooled (He was calmed),
as it is stated: "And he stood among the myrtles
phrases.notes: זכריה 1:8. This is the same vision quoted in Step 4.

phrases.english: that were in the depths."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the vision. After the red horse (anger), we now learn what calmed ה׳.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'standing among the myrtles in the depths' mean in זכריה's vision?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ looked at the צדיקים in בבל and was calmed.

steps.title: Proving that myrtles mean צדיקים and the depths mean בבל
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים prove the meaning of the words. 'Myrtles' means צדיקים, because אסתר is called הדסה. 'The depths' means בבל, because ישעיהו calls בבל 'the deep'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Myrtles' always means righteous people, as it says: 'And he raised הדסה.' 'The depths' always means בבל, as it says: 'He who says to the deep: Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the reading from Step 8 by proving what two words mean. Each word gets its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 needs two facts: 'myrtles' must mean צדיקים, and 'the depths' must mean בבל. הדסה is a name of the צדיקה אסתר, so myrtles stand for צדיקים. The 'deep' that ישעיהו says will be dried up is בבל. Together, the vision means ה׳ looked at the צדיקים living in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: This word means nothing other than...

phrases.english: And "myrtles" means nothing but the righteous,
as it is stated: "And he raised Hadassah."
phrases.notes: אסתר 2:7. הדסה is אסתר, a צדיקה.

phrases.english: And "the depths" means nothing but Babylonia,
as it is stated: "That says to the deep: Be dry,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 44:27

phrases.english: and I will dry up your rivers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the meaning of the two key words used in Step 8.

steps.title: The angry horses change color
steps.stepSummary: Right away, the horses that were full of anger turned gray, and the red ones turned white.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, the ones full of anger became gray, and the red ones became white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of the vision: the different horse colors. These colors show that ה׳'s anger went away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, red stood for ה׳'s wish to turn the world into blood. Once ה׳ was calmed, the colors softened. Red became white, and angry became gray. The color change in the vision matches the calming of ה׳'s anger.

phrases.english: Immediately, those full of anger became gray,
phrases.notes: These are the horses in זכריה's vision, which were red, gray and white.

phrases.english: and the red ones became white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of ה׳ being calmed: the horses' colors change.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gray and white horses in the vision show that the anger turned into calm.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole vision tells one story. ה׳ was angry (night, red horse), He looked at the צדיקים in בבל, and He calmed down (white horses).

steps.title: A white horse in a dream is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from the vision that seeing a white horse in a dream is a good sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We learn from this that a white horse is good for a dream.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a practical lesson from the vision about what dreams mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vision, white horses appeared when ה׳'s anger turned into calm. So white horses are connected with peace. That is why seeing one in a dream is a good sign.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
Conclude from it
that a white horse is good for a dream.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical lesson from the white horses in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing a white horse in a dream is a good sign.

steps.title: What happened to חנניה מישאל ועזריה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where חנניה מישאל ועזריה went after the miracle, since we never hear about them again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis, where did they go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It is setting up the opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the furnace miracle, the תנ״ך never mentions חנניה מישאל ועזריה again. The גמרא wants to know what became of them.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, where did they go?
phrases.notes: 'The Rabbis' here means חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the vision and asks a new question about the three צדיקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What happened to חנניה מישאל ועזריה after the miracle?

steps.title: Three answers: evil eye, spit, or a happy life in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב says they died from עין הרע. שמואל says they drowned in spit. רבי יוחנן says they went up to ארץ ישראל, married, and had children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They died from the evil eye. שמואל said: They drowned in spit. רבי יוחנן said: They went up to ארץ ישראל, married women, and had sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question from Step 12, and each one gives a different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב: people were jealous of their miracle, and that jealousy (עין הרע) killed them. שמואל: they 'drowned in spit', meaning they were overwhelmed by the scorn of the nations. רבי יוחנן: nothing bad happened. They simply moved to ארץ ישראל and built families.

keyTerms.meaning: The evil eye; harm caused by jealousy

phrases.english: Rav says: They died from the evil eye.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: They drowned in spit.
phrases.notes: He means the spit of the nations, who looked down on the Jews.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: עָלוּ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: They went up to Eretz Yisrael,
and married women and had sons and daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They died from עין הרע (רב), drowned in spit (שמואל), or settled in ארץ ישראל and had families (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: The same three opinions among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The same argument already appears among the תנאים: רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches a dispute among the תנאים. רבי אליעזר says: They died from the evil eye. רבי יהושע says: They drowned in spit. The חכמים say: They went up to ארץ ישראל, married women, and had sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument between the אמוראים in Step 13 already existed earlier, among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each אמורא's view matches one תנא. רב matches רבי אליעזר, שמואל matches רבי יהושע, and רבי יוחנן matches the חכמים. So none of the three views is new. Each has older support.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute among the תנאים

phrases.english: This is like a dispute among the tanna'im:
Rabbi Eliezer says: They died from the evil eye.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: They drowned in spit.
And the Rabbis say: They went up to Eretz Yisrael
and married women and had sons and daughters,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the three opinions of Step 13 match an earlier argument among the תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between the אמוראים follows the same lines as the argument between the תנאים.

steps.title: The פסוק behind the חכמים: 'men of wonder'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים prove their view from a פסוק in זכריה. יהושע the כהן גדול's friends are called 'men of wonder', and that must mean חנניה מישאל ועזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Hear now, יהושע the כהן גדול, you and your friends who sit before you, for they are men of wonder.' Who are the people for whom a wonder was done? You must say it is חנניה, מישאל and עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the חכמים' view that the three went up to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע the כהן גדול lived in ארץ ישראל after the return from בבל. His friends are called 'men of wonder'. The only people of that time who had a miracle done for them were חנניה מישאל ועזריה. So they must have been in ארץ ישראל, sitting with יהושע, which means they were alive and settled there.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say; it can only be

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the happy ending (רבי יוחנן and the חכמים) has a פסוק behind it. The other two views are not shown with a source here.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Hear now, Joshua the High Priest,
phrases.notes: זכריה 3:8

phrases.english: you and your friends who sit before you,
for they are men of wonder."
Who are the people
for whom a wonder was done?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה חֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: You must say: this is Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports the חכמים' view in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: חנניה מישאל ועזריה went up to ארץ ישראל and lived there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 3:8, 'men of wonder' who sat before יהושע the כהן גדול.

steps.title: Where was דניאל during the furnace story?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where דניאל went, since he was not thrown into the furnace with the other three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And דניאל, where did he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second new question. It is setting up three answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דניאל would never have bowed to the idol. Yet he is not in the furnace story. So he must have been away from בבל at the time, and the גמרא asks where he was.

keyTerms.meaning: דניאל, the friend of the three צדיקים

phrases.english: And Daniel, where did he go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After asking about the three, the גמרא asks about their friend דניאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why was דניאל not in the furnace story, and where was he?

steps.title: Three answers: digging a river, getting seeds, or getting pigs
steps.stepSummary: רב says דניאל went to dig a great river in טבריה. שמואל says he went to bring alfalfa seed. רבי יוחנן says he went to bring pigs from אלכסנדריה in מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: To dig the great river in טבריה. שמואל said: To bring alfalfa seed. רבי יוחנן said: To bring the pigs of אלכסנדריה of מצרים.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question from Step 16. Each says דניאל was away on a different trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three agree on the main point: דניאל was away from בבל. They only argue about what the trip was for: digging a river, bringing alfalfa seed, or bringing pigs.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב: לְמִיכְרֵא נַהֲרָא רַבָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא.
phrases.english: Rav says: To dig the great river in Tiberias.
And Shmuel says: To bring alfalfa seed.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: To bring the pigs
of Alexandria of Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב: לְמִיכְרֵא נַהֲרָא רַבָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 with three opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דניאל was away digging a river (רב), bringing alfalfa seed (שמואל), or bringing pigs from אלכסנדריה (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: Challenge: אלכסנדריה never let breeding animals leave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with a ברייתא. Every cow and pig leaving אלכסנדריה had its womb cut so it could not give birth. So why would anyone travel there for pigs?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But a ברייתא teaches: תודוס the doctor said, no cow or pig leaves אלכסנדריה of מצרים unless they cut its womb so it cannot give birth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 17 using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people of אלכסנדריה wanted to keep their special breed for themselves. So they made every animal that left unable to give birth. That makes it pointless for דניאל to go there to bring back pigs to breed, so רבי יוחנן's answer seems wrong.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But isn't it taught: Theodosius the doctor says,
no cow or sow goes out
from Alexandria of Egypt
without them cutting its womb
phrases.notes: Literally 'its mother'. Here that means the womb.

phrases.english: so that it will not give birth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that דניאל went to bring pigs from אלכסנדריה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animals leaving אלכסנדריה could not breed, so there was no reason to go there to get them.

steps.title: Answer: he took young pigs secretly
steps.stepSummary: דניאל brought small pigs without the people of אלכסנדריה knowing, so their wombs were never cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought small ones without their knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and saves רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about cutting the womb only worked when the people of אלכסנדריה knew an animal was leaving. דניאל took young pigs secretly, so they were never cut and could still breed. The ברייתא and רבי יוחנן no longer clash.
steps.whatToRemember: All three answers agree that דניאל was away from בבל during the furnace story. רבי יוחנן's pig answer survives the challenge, because the young pigs were taken secretly.

phrases.english: He brought small ones
without their knowledge.
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the people of אלכסנדריה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ברייתא's rule did not apply to these animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No breeding animals could ever leave אלכסנדריה, so the trip made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: דניאל secretly took young pigs that had not been cut, so they could still breed.

steps.title: Three wanted דניאל away, and ה׳'s reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says three parties agreed that דניאל should be away. הקדוש ברוך הוא's reason was so no one would credit the miracle to דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Three were part of that plan: הקדוש ברוך הוא, דניאל, and נבוכדנצר. הקדוש ברוך הוא said: Let דניאל go from here, so people won't say that the others were saved in his merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining why דניאל was not at the furnace. It begins with the first of three reasons, which is ה׳'s reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 told us where דניאל went. Now we learn why he had to be gone. If דניאל had been there, people would say חנניה מישאל ועזריה were saved only because of his greatness, and not because of their own righteousness.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Three were part of that plan:
phrases.notes: The plan was to have דניאל away when his three friends were thrown into the furnace.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, Daniel, and Nebuchadnezzar.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let Daniel go from here,
so that they will not say: they were saved in his merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה הָיוּ בְּאוֹתָהּ עֵצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning where דניאל went, we now learn why he needed to be away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ kept דניאל away so the miracle would be credited to חנניה מישאל ועזריה themselves.

steps.title: דניאל's own reason for leaving
steps.stepSummary: דניאל feared that he would be burned like an idol, because נבוכדנצר had worshipped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And דניאל said: I will go from here, so that the פסוק 'The images of their gods you shall burn in fire' will not be fulfilled through me.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the second reason, which is דניאל's own reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נבוכדנצר bowed down to דניאל, דניאל worried he might be treated like an idol. The תורה says idols are to be burned, so he could end up in the fire. The proof that נבוכדנצר bowed to him comes in Step 24.

phrases.english: And Daniel said: I will go from here,
so that it will not be fulfilled in me:
"The graven images of their gods you shall burn in fire."
phrases.notes: דברים 7:25.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second of the three reasons listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דניאל left so he would not be burned as if he were an idol.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר's reason for sending דניאל away
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר did not want people saying he burned his own god.
steps.simpleTranslation: And נבוכדנצר said: Let דניאל go from here, so people won't say, 'He burned his god in fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the third and final reason, which is נבוכדנצר's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר treated דניאל like a god. If דניאל refused to bow to the idol and was thrown into the furnace, it would be embarrassing for נבוכדנצר to be known as the king who burned his own god.
steps.whatToRemember: All three parties wanted דניאל away. ה׳ wanted the miracle credited to the three friends. דניאל feared being burned like an idol. נבוכדנצר didn't want to be known for burning his own god.

phrases.english: And Nebuchadnezzar said:
Daniel should go from here,
so that they will not say:
"He burned his god in fire."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third of the three reasons listed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוכדנצר sent דניאל away to avoid the shame of burning the one he worshipped.

steps.title: How do we know נבוכדנצר bowed to דניאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that נבוכדנצר worshipped דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that he bowed to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for something the last two reasons assumed: that נבוכדנצר worshipped דניאל. This question sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both דניאל's fear and נבוכדנצר's worry depend on the idea that נבוכדנצר treated דניאל like a god. The גמרא wants a פסוק to show this really happened.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he bowed to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the assumption in Steps 21 and 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that נבוכדנצר worshipped דניאל.

steps.title: The פסוק showing נבוכדנצר bowed to דניאל
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ספר דניאל says נבוכדנצר fell on his face and bowed to דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Then King נבוכדנצר fell on his face and bowed to דניאל, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a פסוק that describes נבוכדנצר bowing to דניאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says plainly that the king bowed to דניאל. This backs up both דניאל's fear of being treated like an idol and נבוכדנצר's worry about burning 'his god.'

phrases.english: As it is written:
"Then King Nebuchadnezzar
fell on his face
and bowed to Daniel, etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל 2:46.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 with a פסוק.

steps.title: The פסוקים about the false prophets אחאב and צדקיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two פסוקים in ירמיהו about two false prophets whom the king of בבל burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So says ה׳ of hosts, God of ישראל, about אחאב son of קוליה and צדקיהו son of מעשיה, who prophesy falsely to you in My name, etc.' And it is written: 'And a curse will be taken from them by all the exiles of יהודה in בבל, saying: May ה׳ make you like צדקיהו and like אחאב, whom the king of בבל roasted in fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related story about others whom נבוכדנצר put in fire. It quotes the פסוקים to set up a lesson from their exact wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike חנניה מישאל ועזריה, these two men were not saved from the fire. The key word to notice is 'קָלָם' (roasted) in the second פסוק, because the גמרא will build on it next.
steps.confusionAlert: This צדקיהו is a false prophet, the son of מעשיה. He is not צדקיהו the king of יהודה.

phrases.english: "So says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel,
concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah
and concerning Zedekiah son of Maaseiah,
who prophesy to you falsely in My name, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 29:21.

phrases.english: And it is written:
"And from them a curse shall be taken

phrases.aramaic: לְכֹל גָּלוּת יְהוּדָה אֲשֶׁר בְּבָבֶל לֵאמֹר
phrases.english: by all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylonia, saying:
May the Lord make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab,
whom the king of Babylonia roasted in fire."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 29:22.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל אַחְאָב בֶּן קוֹלָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic: people whom נבוכדנצר put in fire and who were not saved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים describe the king of בבל roasting the false prophets אחאב and צדקיהו.

steps.title: 'Roasted,' not 'burned': they were made like toasted grain
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses 'קָלָם' instead of 'שְׂרָפָם,' and רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי says this teaches that they were roasted like grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not say 'whom he burned,' but 'whom he roasted.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: This teaches that he made them like roasted grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices the unusual word in the פסוק. רבי יוחנן explains what it teaches about how the false prophets died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal word for burning is 'שרף.' The פסוק instead chose 'קלה,' the word used for toasting grain. רבי שמעון בן יוחי learns from this that they were roasted like toasted kernels.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not say X, but rather Y

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way the גמרא reads פסוקים: when the פסוק picks an unusual word over the expected one, that choice carries a lesson.

phrases.english: "Whom he burned" is not stated,
but rather "whom he roasted."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
This teaches that he made them like roasted grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשֶׁר שְׂרָפָם לֹא נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא אֲשֶׁר קָלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the exact wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'קָלָם' teaches that נבוכדנצר roasted the false prophets like toasted grain.

steps.title: What exactly did the false prophets do?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing the false prophets' sin and asks what they actually did.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says they did a disgraceful thing in ישראל and committed adultery with their neighbors' wives. What did they do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the פסוק in ירמיהו and asks what real event it is describing. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the king of בבל burned these two prophets, and step 26 explained how. Now the גמרא wants the reason: the פסוק mentions adultery, and the גמרא asks for the actual story behind those words.

phrases.english: "Because they have committed baseness in Israel
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 29:23

phrases.english: and have committed adultery with the wives of their neighbors."
What did they do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how the prophets were punished to why they were punished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real event behind the פסוק's words about adultery.

steps.title: The prophets approach נבוכדנצר's daughter with fake prophecies
steps.stepSummary: אחאב and צדקיה each told נבוכדנצר's daughter that God commanded her to give herself to the other. She told her father, and he told her to send them to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They went to נבוכדנצר's daughter. אחאב told her, 'God says: give yourself to צדקיה.' צדקיה told her, 'God says: give yourself to אחאב.' She went and told her father. He said: 'The God of these people hates immorality. When they come to you, send them to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a story. The two prophets used made-up prophecies to try to seduce the king's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each prophet 'prophesied' on behalf of the other, so the lie would look like it came from two separate prophets. Even נבוכדנצר saw it was false, because he knew the God of ישראל hates immorality.

phrases.english: They went to the daughter of Nebuchadnezzar.
Ahab said to her:
"So says the Lord: Submit to Zedekiah."
phrases.notes: "Submit" here means give herself to him, to be with him.

phrases.english: And Zedekiah said:
"So says the Lord: Submit to Ahab."
She went and told it to her father.
He said to her: The God of these people
hates lewdness.
When they come to you, send them to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They used false prophecies to try to seduce נבוכדנצר's daughter.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר challenges the prophets
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר asks who told them to do this. They say הקדוש ברוך הוא, and he objects that חנניה מישאל ועזריה told him it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came to her, she sent them to her father. He asked them, 'Who told you to do this?' They said, 'הקדוש ברוך הוא.' He said, 'But I asked חנניה מישאל ועזריה, and they told me it is forbidden!'
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, נבוכדנצר questions the prophets and challenges their claim. He uses what other true prophets told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophets claim God's authority. נבוכדנצר answers that three proven righteous men said the opposite, so their claim does not add up.

keyTerms.meaning: The three righteous men from ספר דניאל

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתוֹ לְגַבַּהּ, שַׁדַּרְתַּנְהוּ לְגַבֵּי אֲבוּהָ.
phrases.english: When they came to her, she sent them to her father.
He said to them: Who told you to do this?
They said: The Holy One, Blessed be He.
But I asked Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
and they told me: It is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story continues as נבוכדנצר confronts the prophets.
steps.kashyaTarget: The prophets' claim that God commanded the act.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Proven righteous prophets said it is forbidden, so this claim contradicts them.

steps.title: The prophets claim God told them, not the others
steps.stepSummary: The false prophets answer that they are prophets too, and God simply gave this message to them and not to חנניה מישאל ועזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him, 'We are also prophets like them. God did not tell it to them; He told it to us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The false prophets try to push back against נבוכדנצר's challenge. They say they have their own prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They do not deny what חנניה מישאל ועזריה said. Instead, they claim equal standing and say they got a private message the others did not get.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֲנַן נָמֵי נְבִיאֵי כְּוָותַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: They said to him: We too are prophets like them.
To them He did not say it;
to us He said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוכדנצר's challenge from step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Claim of a separate, private prophecy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבוכדנצר assumed the true prophets' ruling settles the matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prophets claim God told only them.

steps.title: נבוכדנצר decides to test them
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר says he will test them the same way he tested חנניה מישאל ועזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them, 'I want to test you, just like I tested חנניה מישאל ועזריה.'
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר answers their claim by setting up a test. This prepares the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If they really are prophets 'like them,' they should pass the same test. The test was the fiery furnace, where חנניה מישאל ועזריה were saved.

phrases.english: He said to them: I want to test you,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּבְדַקְתִּינְהוּ לַחֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: just as I tested Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
phrases.notes: He means the fiery furnace in דניאל chapter 3, where they came out unharmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the prophets' claim by demanding proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophets will face the same furnace test as חנניה מישאל ועזריה.

steps.title: The prophets choose יהושע כהן גדול to join them
steps.stepSummary: The prophets complain that the others were three and they are only two. נבוכדנצר lets them pick a third, and they pick יהושע כהן גדול, hoping his merit will protect them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said, 'They were three, and we are only two.' He said, 'Choose whoever you want to be with you.' They said, 'יהושע כהן גדול.' They thought: let יהושע come, because his merit is great and it will protect us.
steps.whatsHappening: The prophets try to improve their chances before the test. They bring along a righteous man to shield them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their complaint suggests that three people together have more merit than two. They are not trusting their own merit; they are hoping to hide behind יהושע's merit.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִינּוּן תְּלָתָא הֲווֹ, וַאֲנַן תְּרֵין.
phrases.english: They said to him: They were three, and we are two.
He said to them: Choose for yourselves
whoever you want to be with you.
They said: Joshua the High Priest.
They thought: Let Joshua come,
since his merit is great and it will protect us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The prophets respond to the test of step 31 by asking for a third person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע כהן גדול is added to the test, chosen for his protective merit.

steps.title: The result: the prophets burn, יהושע is only singed
steps.stepSummary: All three were thrown into the furnace. The two false prophets were burned, and יהושע כהן גדול's clothes were singed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought them down and threw them in. The prophets were burned up. יהושע כהן גדול's clothes were singed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the result of the test. The false prophets die, and יהושע survives with only his clothes singed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects back to step 26, where the פסוק said the king 'roasted' them. יהושע's merit saved him but did not save the prophets, and his clothes were still harmed.

phrases.english: They brought them down and threw them in.
They were burned,

phrases.aramaic: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל אִיחֲרֻךְ אִיחֲרוֹכֵי מָאנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and Joshua the High Priest's garments were singed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the outcome of the test set up in steps 31 and 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The false prophets were burned; יהושע's clothes were singed.

steps.title: פסוקים in זכריה hint that יהושע was saved from fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two פסוקים in זכריה about יהושע כהן גדול standing before an angel, with God rebuking the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He showed me יהושע the High Priest standing before the angel of God...' And it says: 'God said to the שטן: God will rebuke you...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the story of יהושע from פסוקים in זכריה. It shows that יהושע was rescued from a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second פסוק continues with 'Is this not a firebrand rescued from fire?' That describes יהושע as a burning stick pulled out of the fire, matching the story that he was saved with only singed clothes.
steps.whatToRemember: אחאב and צדקיה lied in God's name to seduce the king's daughter. Even with יהושע כהן גדול beside them, they burned, while יהושע came out with only singed clothes. The words 'firebrand rescued from fire' in זכריה are the hint.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And He showed me Joshua the High Priest
standing before the angel of the Lord, etc."
phrases.notes: זכריה 3:1

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the Lord said to Satan:
The Lord shall rebuke you, etc."
phrases.notes: זכריה 3:2. The "etc." points to the rest of the פסוק: "Is this not a firebrand rescued from fire?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the outcome of step 33 with פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושע כהן גדול was in a fire and was rescued.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זכריה 3:1-2, especially the phrase 'a firebrand rescued from fire.'

steps.title: Why did the fire touch you at all?
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר asks יהושע כהן גדול: if you are righteous, why did the fire singe you, when חנניה מישאל ועזריה were not touched at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I know you are a צדיק. But why did the fire affect you a little? It did not affect חנניה מישאל ועזריה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר compares יהושע to חנניה מישאל ועזריה and asks why he was not saved as completely as they were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר accepts that יהושע is righteous, because he survived. But his clothes were singed, while the earlier three came out with nothing burned. That gap needs an explanation.

phrases.english: He said to him: I know that you are righteous,
phrases.notes: נבוכדנצר is speaking to יהושע כהן גדול.

phrases.english: but what is the reason
that the fire had a little effect on you?
Chananiah, Mishael and Azariah —
it had no effect on them at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי טַעְמָא אַהְנְיָא בָּךְ פּוּרְתָּא נוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up from the furnace story: why was יהושע singed?
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that a צדיק was partly burned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the earlier furnace incident, חנניה מישאל ועזריה were not touched at all, so why was he singed?

steps.title: They were three, I was one
steps.stepSummary: יהושע answers that חנניה מישאל ועזריה were three together, while he was alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They were three, and I am one.
steps.whatsHappening: יהושע gives his first answer: the three had more combined merit than one person alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a group of צדיקים has stronger protection than a single person. That would explain why he was slightly harmed and they were not.

phrases.english: He said to him: They were three,
and I am one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נבוכדנצר's question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every צדיק should be fully protected
steps.terutzMaskana: Three צדיקים together have more protection than one

steps.title: But אברהם was alone
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר objects: אברהם was only one person, and the fire did not hurt him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But wasn't אברהם alone?
steps.whatsHappening: נבוכדנצר challenges the 'three versus one' answer with the case of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was alone in the fire and was not harmed at all. So being only one person cannot be the reason יהושע was singed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא אַבְרָהָם יָחִיד הֲוָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't Abraham one person?
phrases.notes: He means that אברהם was also thrown into a furnace, and came out unharmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one person alone gets less protection
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אברהם was alone and was fully protected

steps.title: The wicked men with me gave the fire permission
steps.stepSummary: יהושע explains that אברהם had no רשעים with him, but he was thrown in together with wicked men, so the fire was allowed to burn.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, no wicked people were with him, so the fire was not given permission. Here, wicked people were with me, so the fire was given permission.
steps.whatsHappening: יהושע gives a new answer. The difference is not how many צדיקים there were, but whether רשעים were present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the fire burns רשעים, it has permission to do harm, and a צדיק standing next to them can be partly hurt. אברהם was alone with no רשעים, so the fire had no permission at all.
steps.whatToRemember: A צדיק standing next to רשעים can be harmed along with them, because the punishment has been given permission to act.

phrases.english: There, there were no wicked people with him,
and permission was not given to the fire.
Here, there were wicked people with me,
phrases.notes: The wicked people are the two false prophets who burned.

phrases.english: and permission was given to the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from אברהם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference was the number of צדיקים
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference was that רשעים were present, which gave the fire permission to burn

steps.title: Two dry sticks burn the wet one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports this idea with a popular saying: two dry logs set fire to one wet log.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what people say: two dry firebrands and one wet one, the dry ones set the wet one on fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up יהושע's answer with a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wet log does not usually burn by itself, but next to dry logs it catches fire. In the same way, the צדיק (the wet log) was singed because he was next to the two רשעים (the dry logs).

phrases.english: This is what people say:
Two dry firebrands and one wet one,
the dry ones burn the wet one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer just given
steps.raayaObject: A צדיק can be harmed when he is next to רשעים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying about dry and wet firebrands

steps.title: Why was יהושע punished at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what sin caused יהושע כהן גדול to be punished with the furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason he was punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question. Even if being near רשעים explains the singeing, a צדיק still needs some reason to be punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being next to רשעים explains how the fire could reach him, but not why he deserved it. The גמרא wants to find the actual fault.

phrases.english: What is the reason he was punished?
phrases.notes: 'He' is יהושע כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the story by asking for the cause of his punishment
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin of יהושע caused his punishment

steps.title: His sons married women unfit for כהונה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says יהושע's sons married women who were not fit to marry כהנים, and he did not protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because his sons were marrying women who were unfit for כהונה, and he did not protest against them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: יהושע was punished for not stopping his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin was not something יהושע did himself. It was his failure to object to what his sons were doing.
steps.whatToRemember: A person can be held responsible for wrongdoing he could have protested and did not.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because his sons were marrying women
who were not fit for the priesthood,
and he did not protest against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שֶׁהָיוּ בָּנָיו נוֹשְׂאִין נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He failed to protest his sons' improper marriages

steps.title: The 'filthy clothes' in זכריה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says יהושע wore filthy clothes. He would not really dress that way, so the clothes hint at his sons' improper marriages.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And יהושע was dressed in filthy clothes.' Was it יהושע's way to wear filthy clothes? Rather, this teaches that his sons married women unfit for כהונה, and he did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול would not really wear dirty clothes, so the words cannot be read simply. The 'filth' is a hint to the stain his sons' marriages left on him.

phrases.english: As it says: 'And Joshua was dressed in filthy clothes.'
phrases.notes: זכריה 3:3

phrases.english: Was it the way of Joshua
to wear filthy clothes?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ בָּנָיו נוֹשְׂאִים נָשִׁים
phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that his sons were marrying women
who were not fit for the priesthood,
and he did not protest against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ הָיָה לָבֻשׁ בְּגָדִים צוֹאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב פפא's answer
steps.raayaObject: יהושע's sons married improperly and he did not protest

steps.title: What were the 'six barley grains'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום reports that בר קפרא taught in ציפורי about the פסוק in רות: 'These six barley grains he gave me.' What does that mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said: בר קפרא taught in ציפורי: What is the meaning of 'These six barley grains he gave me'? What are the 'six barley grains'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. The גמרא is setting up a question about the meaning of a פסוק in רות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are רות's words to נעמי about the gift from בועז. The phrase 'six barley grains' sounds odd, so בר קפרא asks what it really means.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said:
Bar Kappara taught in Tzippori:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'These six barley grains he gave me'?
phrases.notes: רות 3:17

phrases.english: What are 'six barley grains'?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ בַּר קַפָּרָא בְּצִיפּוֹרִי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new derashah. It is still part of the larger discussion of חנניה מישאל ועזריה, but it does not answer the previous question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'six barley grains' in רות 3:17

steps.title: Not six actual grains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the literal reading: בועז would not give a gift of just six grains of barley.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means six actual grains of barley, is it בועז's way to give a gift of six grains?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simple meaning and pushes it away, setting up a deeper explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six grains is a worthless gift, and a generous man like בועז would not give it. So the words must hint at something else.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the פסוק is wrong. It is only ruling out the literal reading so it can explain what the words hint at.

phrases.english: If you say six actual barley grains,
is it the way of Boaz
to give a gift of six barley grains?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one possible answer to the question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The literal reading of 'six barley grains'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such a tiny gift does not fit בועז's character
